headline: Traffic-led sales growth; tariff reinvestment hits margin
summary_short: Dollar Tree's Q3 net sales rose 6.9% to $5.1B on comparable sales up 4.6%, but operating income fell 10.1% to $309M as tariff reinvestment cost 195bp of margin. FY26 adjusted EPS outlook was raised to $8.05-$8.25.
summary_long: Comparable sales rose 4.6% (traffic +3.8%, ticket +0.8%). Operating margin contracted 110bp, including a 195bp cost from net tariff reinvestments. Diluted EPS was $1.24 and adjusted EPS $1.16, each including a $0.42 cost from tariff reinvestment. Operating cash flow was $375M, free cash flow $122M; $205M of shares were repurchased. Q4 outlook: comps +3% to +4%, adjusted EPS $2.46-$2.66.
confidence_notes: Results are on a continuing-operations basis (Dollar Tree U.S. and Canada banners). Adjusted EPS and margin figures include company-stated tariff refund and reinvestment effects. The release does not state prior-year EPS in the portion read, so EPS has no delta.

drivers.explanation: Growth came from a 3.8% increase in traffic and a 0.8% increase in average ticket; the CEO cites a broader assortment and better stores.
Tariff refund reinvestment totaled $103M, including a $40M charitable donation within SG&A; SG&A rose 70bp to 29.9% of revenue and gross margin fell 10bp to 35.7%.
Management raised the full-year adjusted EPS outlook, which includes an approximate $0.65 benefit from net tariff refunds.
